transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, it's probably nothing too serious, but I actually ended up calling the EAP at work to see someone. I supervise a sales team, so the office is always pretty lively, which is usually fine, but... lately, I guess I've been a little on edge? Like, every little bang in the office just really gets to me. If someone just shuts a file drawer, or... or drops a coffee mug, I just jump so hard. And then my chest just keeps racing for way longer than it probably should. 

I know it sounds kind of silly, getting startled over normal office stuff, and I'm sure I'm just overreacting a bit, but... I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling anxious or worried when there aren't any sudden noises or surprises?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really don't want to make it sound like a bigger deal than it is. But, yeah, lately when I'm in the office, I find myself kind of... keeping track of everything? 

Like, I just keep checking where my boss is, or... or where the exits are. And I'm always looking over my shoulder to see if anyone is coming up behind me. I catch myself doing it even when I'm supposed to be right there, focused on my team. I tell myself it's just me trying to be aware of my surroundings, you know, being a good supervisor? I hope that doesn't make me sound completely paranoid. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you feel anxious or on edge when you're not at the office?

Um, outside the office? I mean, I think I'm mostly okay. I really try to just leave work at work, you know? 

I guess... well, I might still be a tiny bit jumpy if a car backfires or something loud happens, but I think that's pretty normal, right? Everyone gets startled by loud noises. I definitely don't feel like I'm constantly checking the exits when I'm just at home or at the grocery store. I try to just relax when I'm off the clock. So, I think I'm doing okay outside of work. Does that sound alright? I hope I'm explaining this well enough.
Do you ever find yourself worrying about things when you're alone and there's nothing immediately stressful happening?

Um, no, not really. I mean, when I'm alone, I usually just try to unwind, you know? Put on a show or listen to some music. 

I don't think I sit around worrying about things when it's quiet. I try to be pretty positive and just enjoy the downtime. I mean, everyone has a passing thought now and then about, like, paying bills or whatever, but nothing major. I definitely wouldn't say I'm a worrier or anything like that. I just try to take it easy. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just trying not to dwell on things when I don't have to?
Have you been avoiding any places or situations because of how they might make you feel?

Um, avoiding places? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still go to work every day, and I still go to the store and all my normal spots. 

I guess... well, I try to stay away from the breakroom at work if it's really crowded and noisy, but I think that's just because I like to have a quiet lunch, you know? It's not like I'm scared to go in there or anything. I just prefer to eat at my desk where I can catch up on emails and be productive. That's a pretty normal thing for a supervisor to do, right? Just trying to stay focused and not get distracted by all the chatter? I definitely wouldn't say I'm avoiding anything, just... managing my time well, I hope?
Do you feel like you're able to fully relax and calm down when you're not at work or in a potentially noisy environment?

Um, yeah, I think so. I mean, when I get home, I really try to just kick back. 

I guess sometimes it takes a little bit to wind down after a long day, but that's just because I'm thinking about, you know, making sure my team is set up for tomorrow. But once I'm settled in, I feel like I can relax just fine. I might keep the TV volume a little low just so it's peaceful, but that's just because I like a calm environment, right? It's good to have a quiet space to recharge. So yeah, I'd say I can relax pretty well. I'm doing the right things to take care of myself, don't you think?
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

Um, intense fear? No, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I mean, I've been startled before, like if someone drops something heavy or a car honks too loud, but that's just a normal reaction, isn't it? 

I definitely haven't had any sudden, overwhelming panic or anything that peaks like you're saying. If things get a little stressful, I just take a deep breath and handle it. That's the best way to deal with things, right? Just keeping a level head? So, no, I wouldn't say I've ever felt anything like what you're describing. I'm doing pretty well with keeping things in perspective, I think.
Do you feel anxious or on edge even on your days off from work?

Um, on my days off? No, not really. I mean, weekends are my time to just, you know, decompress. 

I guess sometimes I might feel a little... keyed up on a Saturday morning, but that's just because I'm used to being on the go all week, right? It takes a second to shift gears from being a supervisor to just being at home. But I wouldn't call it being on edge or anxious. I just like to stay busy, maybe tackle some chores or run errands. Keeping active is a good way to spend a day off, isn't it? It means I'm not just sitting around doing nothing. So, yeah, I feel pretty normal on my days off. I think I balance things out okay, don't you?
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge in completely quiet and safe environments?

Um, no, not really. I mean, quiet places are supposed to be relaxing, right? 

I guess sometimes if it's *too* quiet, my mind might wander a bit, just thinking about work or what I need to do next week. But that's just being proactive, isn't it? It's not like I'm sitting there feeling nervous or anything. I actually really appreciate having a quiet house to myself. It's a healthy way to unwind, don't you think? Just enjoying the peace and quiet? So, no, I definitely don't feel anxious when I'm just hanging out in a safe space. I'm pretty good at leaving work at work, you know?
Can you think of any specific situations or things that make you feel more on edge or anxious?

Um, specific situations? Well, I guess... I mean, the office can be a little distracting lately. 

It's not that I'm anxious, really. It's just, you know, as a supervisor, I like to be aware of my surroundings, right? So, lately, when I'm at my desk, I find myself just... keeping an eye out. Like, I'll check where my boss is, or I'll notice where the exits are, or I'll kind of glance over my shoulder to see if anyone is walking up behind me. Even when I'm supposed to be looking at a report or helping my team. 

But that's just being observant, isn't it? It's good to know what's going on in your workspace, right? I just like to be prepared and stay on top of things. It doesn't mean I'm on edge, I'm just... being thorough. That's a good quality for a supervisor to have, don't you think?
Do you feel like you're anxious or on edge for most of the day, regardless of what you're doing?

Um, most of the day? No, I wouldn't say that at all. 

I mean, sure, there are moments during the day where things get a little busy or stressful, but that's just normal life, right? Everyone has parts of their day where they have to focus a bit more or juggle a few things. But I definitely don't walk around feeling anxious from morning till night. 

Like I said, I have my moments of just being observant at work, but outside of that, I'm pretty relaxed. I can still sit down and watch a game or grab dinner without feeling wound up. I think I handle the day-to-day stuff pretty well, honestly. It's totally normal to not feel perfectly calm every single second of the day, isn't it? I think I'm doing a pretty good job managing it all.
Do you feel like you're often on the lookout for potential threats or dangers, even when there's no obvious reason to be?

Um, well, I guess I sort of mentioned this earlier, but... I don't really see it as looking for *threats*, exactly. That sounds a little extreme, doesn't it? 

But, yeah, like I said before about the office... I do find myself kind of keeping track of things a bit more now. Like, I'll catch myself checking where my boss is sitting, or just making a mental note of where the exits are. And sometimes I'll just glance over my shoulder to see if someone's walking up behind me. Even when I'm supposed to be totally focused on helping my team with their numbers or whatever. 

But I feel like that's just being a responsible supervisor, you know? It's good to be aware of your environment, right? I'm just trying to make sure everything is running smoothly. It's not like I'm paranoid or anything. I just like to be on top of things. That's a totally normal way to work, isn't it?
Do you feel like you're on edge or anxious when you're interacting with your family or close friends?

Um, no, not really. With my family and friends, I'm... I'm pretty much myself. 

I mean, sure, sometimes if we're out somewhere crowded, I might still kind of notice where the doors are, like I do at work. But interacting with *them*? No, they don't make me anxious or on edge at all. We just hang out, you know? Have a few beers, watch the game. It's totally fine. 

I think I'm a pretty relaxed guy to be around, honestly. I definitely don't want to be one of those people who brings their work stress home and takes it out on their family, you know? That's not me at all. I do a good job of keeping things separate, don't you think?
Do you feel like your anxiety or being on edge is mostly related to your work environment or does it happen in other areas of your life as well?

Um, well, like I was saying, it's really just... mostly at work, I guess. 

I mean, I don't even really like calling it "anxiety" or being "on edge." That makes it sound like I'm falling apart, and I'm really not. I'm just... staying alert, you know? Keeping an eye on the office, making sure the team is good, knowing who is coming and going. That's just being a good supervisor. 

Outside of work, like I said, I'm fine. If I'm out at a restaurant or a bar with buddies, sure, I might glance around and notice where the exits are, but that's just common sense, right? It's not like I'm sitting there sweating or freaking out. I'm just being smart about my surroundings. Everyone does that a little bit, don't they? I feel like I'm handling everything pretty well, all things considered.
Do you find yourself being constantly on the lookout for potential threats or dangers, even when you're not at work?

Um, no, not constantly. Like I mentioned, it's really not like that. 

I guess I just... I mean, if I'm at the grocery store or something, I'm just getting my groceries, you know? I'm not scanning the aisles for danger. That would be crazy. I'm just a normal guy doing normal things. 

Like I said before, maybe I just pay a little more attention to where the doors are if it's super crowded, but that's just being safe. It's not like a constant, obsessive thing. I'm definitely not walking around terrified all the time. I'm doing okay, right? It sounds like I'm doing okay.
Do you feel like you're on edge or anxious in most social situations, not just at work?

Um, no, definitely not. I mean, I think I handle social stuff really well, honestly. 

I'm not sitting there shaking or, like, hiding in a corner or anything like that. If I go to a buddy's house or out to grab a bite, I'm just focused on having a good time. I might, you know, just prefer to sit facing the door or something small like that, but it doesn't ruin the night. It's just a preference, really. 

I wouldn't say I'm anxious in most situations at all. I'm pretty easygoing, mostly. That's a good thing, right? Being able to just go out and be normal? I feel like I'm doing a pretty good job of keeping it together.
Do you find yourself being on the lookout for potential threats or dangers even when you are in a completely safe and familiar environment?

Um, well... I mean, safe and familiar, yeah. Like the office. The office is totally safe, right? I've worked there for a while. 

But, um... I guess lately, even when I'm there, I do find myself... just keeping an eye on things a bit more than I used to. Like, instead of just staring at my computer or focusing completely on my team like I'm supposed to, I might... I don't know, just check where my boss is. Or I'll glance at the exits. And I definitely prefer to know if someone is walking up behind me. 

But I think that's just being a proactive supervisor, you know? Just staying aware of the floor. It's not like I'm expecting something terrible to happen. I'm just staying sharp. That makes sense for someone in my position, doesn't it? I'm still getting all my work done, so it's not a big deal, right?
Do you find yourself being on the lookout for potential threats or dangers even when you're alone at home?

Um, no, not really. I mean, home is home, right? It's my place. 

I guess... well, I always lock the doors, obviously. Everyone does that. And maybe I double-check them before I go to bed, just to be sure. But I'm not, like, peeking through the blinds or pacing the halls or anything crazy like that. I just watch TV or play some video games, you know? Just regular stuff to unwind. 

If I hear a weird noise outside, I might mute the TV for a second just to listen, but that's just common sense, isn't it? Better safe than sorry. It doesn't mean I'm scared or anything. I just like to make sure everything is secure so I can relax. That's pretty normal, right? I feel like most guys my age would do the exact same thing.
Do you find yourself being constantly on the lookout for potential threats or dangers even when you're in a very relaxed and comfortable setting?

Um, no, not constantly. Like I said, if I'm comfortable, I'm comfortable. 

Like if I'm just chilling on the couch watching a game or hanging out with my friends, I'm just focused on that. I'm not, you know, scanning the room like a bodyguard or anything. I just want to relax and have a good time like anyone else. 

I might still prefer to sit where I can see the door, like I mentioned before, but that's just a habit, really. It's not like I'm sitting there waiting for something bad to happen. I just feel a little better when I know what's going on around me. That's not a bad thing, is it? Just being a little aware of your surroundings? I think I'm handling everything pretty well, all things considered.
Do you find yourself being on the lookout for potential threats or dangers even when you're not thinking about work or any specific worries?

Um, no, not really. I mean, if I'm not thinking about work or... or anything stressful, I'm usually just trying to enjoy my downtime. 

I don't think I'm constantly on edge or anything. Like, if I'm just out grabbing a coffee or walking to my car, I'm just thinking about regular stuff, you know? What I'm going to eat for dinner, or... or a movie I want to see. I'm not looking over my shoulder every five seconds. 

I guess I'm just a naturally observant guy. I notice things around me, but I wouldn't call it looking for threats. It's just... paying attention to the world, right? That's just a good life skill to have, wouldn't you say? I really think I'm doing okay with all this.
